clearedSpotChecks.check: Faces of the native asset: LegacyERC20ETH. Walk sync, settle, take, mint and burn across address(0) and the legacy id in every order, including the forced ETH route that Lagoon adds on OP Mainnet, public protocol fee collection on OP Mainnet, and zero amounts.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I repeated the chain reads and traced every order myself. On OP Mainnet at block 159916351 eth_getCode at 0xDeadDeAddeAddEAddeadDEaDDEAdDeaDDeAD0000 returned 3,671 bytes, balanceOf(PoolManager) returned 245.490343821894100613 ETH, and eth_getBalance of the PoolManager returned the same number. On Zora at block 54368821 the same address has 3,671 bytes and both reads returned 0.151435021246941935 ETH. With the PoolManager as sender, transfer(address,uint256) with amount 0 and with amount 1 reverted with the string 'LegacyERC20ETH: transfer is disabled' on both chains, and empty calldata reverted with and without 1 wei. The address has no code on Base, Unichain, World Chain, Ink and Soneium, so the item's chain list is right. sync(legacy) on the deployed OP Mainnet PoolManager returned without error. Code reading: sync stores the legacy id and the native balance (src/PoolManager.sol:285-286, src/types/Currency.sol:94, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32). While that id is synced, settle and settleFor revert on any msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:356), and they are the only payable functions in src/ (src/PoolManager.sol:300, 305), so no native payment can be credited as address(0) and then read a second time through the legacy view. A second sync overwrites the single currency slot (src/PoolManager.sol:283, 286) and settle resets it (src/PoolManager.sol:361), so one inflow is credited once. A fall of the native balance after sync(legacy) makes the checked subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360 revert. A legacy credit can only come from ETH forced in at the settler's own cost, and it cannot be paid out because take calls transfer on the legacy contract, which reverts (src/types/Currency.sol:73, 82-86, src/PoolManager.sol:294-295). I also walked the shared transaction case: a sync(legacy) left by an earlier call makes a later settle with value revert, which is the denial already recorded as F-071, and a router that calls sync(address(0)) first clears the slot. I found no order that moves accounted funds. The statement about forced ETH after Lagoon rests on the source of SafeSend on the develop branch, which I fetched (HTTP 200) and which is not deployed today.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Faces of the native asset: the WETH predeploy, after the sixteen shape sweep. Walk the orders that use the fact that WETH accepts every selector and mints to msg.sender on a value call.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I ran my own sequence on all seven chains with a 90 byte stub of my own placed at the PoolManager address by state override, so that every call to WETH came from the PoolManager address inside one eth_call. On each chain a call with 5 wei and empty calldata succeeded with empty return data and raised balanceOf(PoolManager) by exactly 5. transfer of 2 returned a 32 byte 1 and lowered the balance by 2. transfer to the WETH address itself and to the zero address moved the tokens like any transfer and returned no ETH. The unlockCallback and beforeSwap selectors succeeded with empty return data and left the balance unchanged. A transfer of 2^255 reverted. The deployed code is 2,041 bytes on OP Mainnet, Base, Zora and World Chain and 2,865 bytes on Unichain, Ink and Soneium. The PUSH4 selectors I extracted from the code are name, approve, totalSupply, transferFrom, withdraw, decimals, balanceOf, symbol, transfer, deposit and allowance on all seven, plus version on the three larger ones. That is the function list of WETH98.sol and WETH.sol, which I fetched from the develop branch: fallback and receive call deposit for msg.sender, transferFrom needs an allowance from the source, and withdraw pays msg.sender only. Code reading: the PoolManager sends to a currency only transfer and balanceOf (src/types/Currency.sol:60-73, 94), to a recipient only a value call with empty calldata (src/types/Currency.sol:48), to a hook only the IHooks selectors (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134) and to its caller only unlockCallback (src/PoolManager.sol:110). None of these is approve or withdraw, so no third party gains an allowance and no WETH held by the PoolManager can be unwrapped by it. take(address(0), WETH, a) debits the caller a in native before the call (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295) and the minted WETH can be credited once under the WETH id if that id was synced (src/PoolManager.sol:358-364). The caller then holds a WETH credit of a and a native debt of a. The address 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 also fails isValidHookAddress, because bits 1 and 2 are return-delta flags without their action flags (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:112-116), which the item did not mention and which does not change the result.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Cycle 3 gap and leads L-119 and L-214: can an account without a role cause a balance write on a B20 token, which would change the PoolManager's balance outside its own transfer calls (assumption A2).
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched the Stablecoin and Asset logic v3, both dispatch files, the precompile entry points, the macro file and the factory logic at tag v1.5.6 of github.com/base/base (HTTP 200 each). The mainnet.base.org endpoint reports reth/v2.5.2-9e380dd with base/v1.5.6. In b20_stablecoin/logic/v3.rs set_balance is called only in move_balance (lines 112 and 116), burn_inner (line 135) and mint (line 333). transfer passes the caller as source (line 221). transfer_from checks the allowance of the source for the caller before the move (lines 250-258). mint checks the Mint role unless privileged (line 313). burn checks the Burn role and burns the caller's own balance (lines 347-348). burn_blocked checks the BurnBlocked role and ensure_blocked (lines 361-363). seize_with_memo checks the Seize role (line 380). permit recovers an ECDSA signer and compares it with the owner, so a contract address, for which nobody can produce a signature, cannot be the owner of a permit. move_balance reads the recipient balance after it has written the sender balance, so a self transfer does not inflate. The Asset file has the same write sites plus batch_mint behind the Mint role, and balanceOf returns the stored balance. dispatch_with_observer passes privileged = false in both variants. The only caller that passes true is the factory, inside create_b20_decoded, after it has reverted with TokenAlreadyExists for any address that already has code (b20_factory/logic/v1.rs lines 205-212), so the privileged path reaches a new token only. The item did not test one route that I consider the most dangerous for a token implemented in the node: a contract that the PoolManager calls (the unlock callback at src/PoolManager.sol:110, a hook at src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134, a native recipient at src/types/Currency.sol:48) could DELEGATECALL or CALLCODE the token so that the precompile sees the PoolManager as caller. The macro base_precompile in macros.rs rejects every call for which input.is_direct_call() is false with DelegateCallNotAllowed, and all four stateful precompiles (both token variants, the factory and the policy registry) are built with that macro. alloy-evm defines is_direct_call as target_address == bytecode_address (read on the main branch, not at the version Base pins). I tested it on chain at Base block 61205525 on mainnet.base.org and on base.gateway.tenderly.co: with the PoolManager as msg.sender of a helper contract placed by state override, a DELEGATECALL and a CALLCODE of OUSD.transfer(recipient, 1) at 0xB2000000000000000000002fEb517dFeC7415344 each failed with the 4 byte error 0x0d89438e, which is the selector of DelegateCallNotAllowed(), and balanceOf(PoolManager) stayed at 5,322,585.696724 OUSD. A direct transfer of 1 unit from the PoolManager address in the same call returned true and lowered the balance by 1. From an account without a role, transferFrom(PoolManager, self, 1) reverted with an insufficient allowance error, and burn(1) and mint(self, 1) reverted with a missing role error. allowance(PoolManager, that account) is 0. The item is right, and the delegatecall guard should be re-tested on every Base release because about 5.3 million OUSD in the PoolManager depend on that one check.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-333. Which addresses from 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000000 to 0x42000000000000000000000000000000000000ff hold an implementation today, and what each returns to sixteen call shapes with the PoolManager as msg.sender: empty calldata with 0 and with 1 wei, transfer(address,uint256) with amount 0 and 1, balanceOf(PoolManager), the ten IHooks selectors with zeroed arguments, and unlockCallback(bytes). The PoolManager code was replaced by a 36 byte forwarding stub through a state override and the call came from a separate account.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I repeated the sweep with my own stub and my own selector list (the ten IHooks selectors and unlockCallback computed from the signatures in src/interfaces/IHooks.sol, plus empty calldata with 0 and 1 wei, transfer with 0 and 1, and balanceOf) over 0x4200..0000 to 0x4200..00ff on all seven chains, at blocks 159916440 (OP Mainnet), 61206568 (Base), 64683342 (Unichain), 54368939 (Zora), 38048049 (World Chain), 61933344 (Ink) and 31148527 (Soneium). The set of targets that do not revert is the one the item lists: WETH 0x06 for every shape, 0x11, 0x16, 0x19, 0x1a and 0x1b for empty calldata with and without 1 wei, 0x13 for every shape with the 32 byte L1 block number (0x1940351 on OP Mainnet), and 0x42 where it holds code. On OP Mainnet a transfer of 1 at 0x42 returns true because the PoolManager holds OP tokens there. On Zora, World Chain, Ink and Soneium only a transfer of 0 returns true. The implementation slots are set at the addresses the item names, 0x2c and 0x2d are empty on Base, 0x30 is set on Base only, and 0x22 to 0x28 are proxies without implementation everywhere. Sixteen code length readings on Base came back empty in a rate limited batch and read 2,055 bytes when I repeated them one by one. Code reading agrees: a 32 byte word other than 1 fails the check at src/types/Currency.sol:68, a balance that is constant inside a transaction gives paid = 0 at src/PoolManager.sol:360, and a hook answer must start with the called selector (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152). None of 0x06, 0x11, 0x13, 0x16, 0x19, 0x1a, 0x1b or 0x42 passes isValidHookAddress, because each has a return-delta bit without its action bit (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:111-120).

clearedSpotChecks.check: Cycle 2 gap: OP Mainnet had no client reading of its own because the official endpoint reports a dev build.
clearedSpotChecks.note: web3_clientVersion on https://op-pokt.nodies.app returned op-reth/v2.4.2-f863ff4c. In rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs at tag op-reth/v2.4.2 (1,513 lines, HTTP 200) line 388 is journal_mut().commit_tx() at the end of execution_result, line 457 is discard_tx() in discard_and_surface_error, and lines 480 to 491 revert to the first checkpoint, bump the nonce, add the mint and call commit_tx() for a failed deposit. rust/Cargo.toml at the same tag pins revm 41.0.0. In revm's journal (crates/context/src/journal/inner.rs, read on the main branch because I did not find the tag that matches 41.0.0) commit_tx and discard_tx both call transient_storage.clear(). The unlock flag, the deltas and the synced currency of src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-21, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:34-40 and src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32 therefore end with the transaction on this build. The build of the OP Mainnet sequencer is still unknown, as the item says.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Faces: the governance token address 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000042 on Unichain, which has no code while five sibling chains hold token code there.
clearedSpotChecks.note: eth_getCode at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000042 on Unichain returned no code at block 64683342, and all sixteen call shapes from the PoolManager address succeeded with empty return data. sync(0x42) on the deployed Unichain PoolManager reverted in an eth_call, while sync(WETH) returned. Code reading: the transfer path accepts success with empty return data (src/types/Currency.sol:68, 73), so take records a debt and moves nothing (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295). balanceOf is a high level call whose 32 byte return is decoded, so empty return data reverts (src/types/Currency.sol:94). Without settle the only sources of a positive delta are burn of existing claims, pool withdrawals and hook deltas, and each of them is matched by an equal earlier debit (src/PoolManager.sol:181-183, 224-226, 334-335), so no claim or pool balance can exist under that id before code appears there.

leads.question: On every new Base node release and at every fork that adds a B20 logic version or a new stateful precompile: does a DELEGATECALL or CALLCODE to a B20 token, to the B20 factory and to the Policy Registry, made by a contract that the PoolManager has called, still revert, and does the token still take the direct caller as the source of transfer?
leads.why: The PoolManager calls contracts chosen by any account (src/PoolManager.sol:110, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134, src/types/Currency.sol:48). In such a frame msg.sender is the PoolManager. At base v1.5.6 one check in the macro base_precompile (input.is_direct_call()) stops that frame from forwarding the PoolManager's identity into the token, and on 23 November 2026 the PoolManager held 5,322,585 OUSD at 0xB2000000000000000000002fEb517dFeC7415344. A release that drops or bypasses the check would let any account move that balance. The test of this cycle is a single read-only eth_call with two state overrides and can be repeated in seconds.

leads.question: Does revm at the exact version 41.0.0 that op-reth v2.4.2 pins clear transient storage in commit_tx and discard_tx, as the main branch does?
leads.why: The verifier read crates/context/src/journal/inner.rs on the main branch of revm, where both functions call transient_storage.clear(). The file at the pinned version was not read because the matching tag was not identified.
